extracted.intended_audience: advanced high-school and undergraduate students preparing for math contests (USAMO/IMO) and problem-solving enthusiasts
extracted.subtask_description: Worked solutions and key lemmas for advanced trigonometry and geometry problems (many from olympiad contests). Contains explicit inequality statements, lemmas, equality-case characterizations, and multiple proof approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclic sum identity (Lemma)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let ABC be a triangle. Then the cyclic sum sin A(cos A − 2 cos B cos C) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shown by double-angle and addition/subtraction formulas: equivalently 2 cyc sin A cos A = 4 cyc sin A cos B cos C and reduction via sin2A and product-to-sum; used to justify sign in subsequent inequality reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 42(a) — quadratic inequality (Barrow)
rubrics_metrics.description: For real x,y,z and triangle ABC, x^2 + y^2 + z^2 ≥ 2yz cos A + 2zx cos B + 2xy cos C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted as a special case of part (b) with n=1; alternative proof via viewing quadratic in x and showing discriminant ≤ 0 (completing the square) — equality cases characterized later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 42(b) — generalized cosine inequality (Wolstenholme)
rubrics_metrics.description: For integer n≥1 and real x,y,z, x^2 + y^2 + z^2 ≥ 2(−1)^{n+1}( yz cos nA + zx cos nB + xy cos nC ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by completing the square in x and reducing to showing a symmetric quadratic is nonnegative. Uses parity of n: when n even use cos(nA)=cos(nB+nC)=cos nB cos nC − sin nB sin nC to reduce to (y sin nC − z sin nB)^2 ≥ 0; when n odd a similar reduction yields same square. Equality: y sin nC = z sin nB (and cyclic permutations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 42(c) — Bottema inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: y z a^2 + z x b^2 + x y c^2 ≤ R^2 (x + y + z)^2, where a,b,c sides and R circumradius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from part (b) by setting n=2 and using extended law of sines (a/R = 2 sin A). After algebra this reduces to the n=2 case of (b). Equality condition: x/sin2A = y/sin2B = z/sin2C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 42(d) — Oppenheim inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: x a^2 + y b^2 + z c^2 ≥ 4[ABC] sqrt(xy + yz + zx).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtained from (c) by substitution x→x a^2 etc., then algebraic manipulation using Introductory Problem 25(a) and taking square roots. Equality case: x a^2 / sin2A = y b^2 / sin2B = z c^2 / sin2C, equivalently proportions involving side-length expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing-the-square discriminant method (proof tool)
rubrics_metrics.description: For quadratic f(x)=x^2 − 2x(z cos B + y cos C) + y^2 + z^2 − 2yz cos A, the discriminant simplifies to −4(z sin B − y sin C)^2 ≤ 0, so f(x) ≥ 0 for all x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This discriminant estimate proves 42(a) and generalizes to show nonnegativity for the family in (b). The text highlights this approach as 'tricky' but generalizable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 43 — circle inscribed in quadrilateral identity and characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: If a circle ω is inscribed in convex quadrilateral ABCD with center I and (|AI|+|DI|)^2 + (|BI|+|CI|)^2 = (|AB|+|CD|)^2, then ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key inequality to prove for any convex quadrilateral with incenter: (|AI|+|DI|)^2 + (|BI|+|CI|)^2 ≤ (|AB|+|CD|)^2, with equality iff AD ∥ BC and |AB| = |CD|. Multiple solutions presented: technical trig, a more geometric trig approach, and a synthetic-geometric solution. Proofs use tangency points, substitutions |AI|=sec x, |AD|=tan x + tan w, etc., and transform to inequalities in tan and sec; equality characterized by x=w and y=z (i.e., AD ∥ BC and AB=CD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma in Problem 43 (Ptolemy-based relation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ω is inscribed in ABCD and A1,B1,C1,D1 are tangency points with angles a,b,c,d then |BI|^2 + (|AI|/|DI|)·|BI|·|CI| = |AB|·|BC| (an identity labeled (†)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by constructing a point P so triangle ABP ~ DCI, showing PAI B is cyclic and applying Ptolemy; substituting similarity ratios yields the identity. This lemma is used to derive the main inequality by AM–GM comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 44 — bounds for ab+bc+ca−abc under a^2+b^2+c^2+abc=4
rubrics_metrics.description: Given nonnegative a,b,c with a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + abc = 4, show 0 ≤ ab + bc + ca − abc ≤ 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower bound: elementary argument using at least one variable ≤1. Upper bound: three proofs—(1) trig substitution a=2 sin(A/2), etc., and AM-GM manipulations giving ab+bc+ca ≤ 2+abc; (2) trig substitution a=2 cos A for acute triangle and case analysis by angles; (3) algebraic method via solving quadratic in a and bounding via discriminant and simple inequalities. Equality characterizations are provided (e.g., triples (2,0,0) for lower bound; other equality cases described in each method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 45 — tangent/cosine product inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: For s,t,u,v in (0,π/2) with s+t+u+v=π, prove sum over cyclic of (√2 sin s − 1)/cos s ≥ 0 (specific symmetric inequality given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute a=tan s etc., transform to rational symmetric identities a+b+c+d = abc + bcd + cda + dab, derive equalities (a^2+1)/(a+b) = (a+c)(a+d)/(a+b+c+d), sum them, then apply Cauchy–Schwarz to obtain inequality 1/cos s + 1/cos t + 1/cos u + 1/cos v ≤ √2( tan s + tan t + tan u + tan v ), and conclude the desired inequality. The proof uses algebraic manipulations and Cauchy–Schwarz.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 46 — calculator/trig-generation of rationals
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a calculator where only sin, cos, tan, arcsin, arccos, arctan keys work and the display starts at 0, show any positive rational q can be obtained by some finite sequence of button presses (functions in radians, infinite precision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key identities: cos^{-1} sin θ = π/2 − θ, tan(cos^{-1} sin(tan^{-1} x)) = 1/x for x>0, and an identity producing √(x+1) from x: tan(cos^{-1} sin(tan^{-1} √x)) = √(x+1). Using the operations √x → √(x+1) and x → 1/x one inductively constructs rationals: build rationals with prescribed denominators by repeated square-root-plus-one and reciprocal operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 47 — extremal cos-sum given product of tans
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix n≥1. For θ_i in (0,π/2) with tan θ1 ··· tan θn = 2^{n/2}, determine minimum λ such that cos θ1 + ... + cos θn ≤ λ. Answer: λ = √3 for n=1; λ = 3/√3 for n=2 (i.e., 2/√3?), and λ = n−1 for n≥3 (precise values listed in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases: n=1 trivial; n=2 reduce to inequality involving tan^2 and bounding via squaring and algebra to find maximum of cos sum; for n≥3 show λ=n−1 by letting n−1 angles →0 and one →π/2 for lower bound, and prove cos sum ≤ n−1 by bounding cos of three largest angles and reduction to an inequality using AM-GM and case splitting. Equality discussions and explicit constructions for limiting cases included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 48 — trig inequality with cyclic sum of squared sums
rubrics_metrics.description: (sin2B + sin2C)^2 sin A + (sin2C + sin2A)^2 sin B + (sin2A + sin2B)^2 sin C ≤ 12 sin A sin B sin C for acute triangle ABC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two solutions: (1) algebraic: rewrite each term as 4 sin^3 A cos^2(B−C) and show cyclic sum ≤ 12 sinA sinB sinC using identities and Introductory Problem 24(a); equality iff triangle equilateral. (2) geometric approach: relate terms to altitudes and prove lemma |DE| + |DF| ≤ |BC| for altitudes AD,BE,CF (with equality iff AB=AC), then convert to area inequalities and sum cyclically to get result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma for Problem 48 — altitudes distance bound
rubrics_metrics.description: In acute triangle ABC with altitudes AD, BE, CF and feet D,E,F, we have |DE| + |DF| ≤ |BC|; equality iff |AB| = |AC|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: use cyclic quadrilaterals AFDC and angle relations to deduce |DF| = R sin 2B, |DE| = R sin 2C, then algebraic manipulation with sum-to-product gives |BC| − (|DE| + |DF|) = 2R sin A [1 − cos(B−C)] ≥ 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 49 — polygon centers equilateral ⇒ regular hexagons and triangle angles
rubrics_metrics.description: On sides of nonobtuse triangle ABC construct externally a square P4, a regular m-gon Pm, and a regular n-gon Pn with centers forming an equilateral triangle; then m = n = 6 and triangle ABC has angles 90°,45°,45°.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma used: if O inside equilateral triangle XYZ and angles Y O Z = x, Z O X = y, X O Y = z, then |OX|/sin(x−60°) = |OY|/sin(y−60°) = |OZ|/sin(z−60°). Apply to circumcenter O and centers of polygons using sine-law formulas for distances to polygon centers, analyze monotonicity of a function f(x)=sin(x−15°)/sin x on [0,90°] to force equalities and deduce angles; equality/limit analysis gives m=n=6 and stated triangle angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 50 — cosine-ratio squared sum inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: For acute triangle ABC, (cosA/cosB)^2 + (cosB/cosC)^2 + (cosC/cosA)^2 + 8 cosA cosB cosC ≥ 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently rewrite RHS as 4/(cos^2 A + cos^2 B + cos^2 C) and prove inequality (†) (see text). Three approaches given: (1) weighted AM-GM to bound pairwise squared ratios and sum; (2) apply Advanced Problem 42(a) to appropriately chosen substitutions x=cosB/cosC etc. to derive lower bound 4(cos^2 A + cos^2 B + cos^2 C); (3) use a lemma for positive reals a,b,c with abc ≤ 1 that a/b + b/c + c/a ≥ a + b + c (proved via rearrangement) and set a=4 cos^2 A etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 51 — Abel-type summation lemmas for trigonometric sums
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemmas used: (1) discrete summation identity: sum_{k=1}^n a_k b_k = S_n b_n + sum_{k=1}^{n-1} S_k(b_k − b_{k+1}), where S_k = sum_{i=1}^k a_i. (Abel's inequality) If b_1 ≥ ... ≥ b_n ≥ 0 then m b_1 ≤ sum a_k b_k ≤ M b_1 where m,M are min,max of partial sums S_k. (Lemma 3) For x not an even multiple of π and m<n, sum_{k=m+1}^n (sin kx)/k ≤ (1/(m+1))·(sin x /2)^{-1} (precise bound in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These lemmas are applied to bound sums like sum_{k=1}^n sin(kx)/k. Proofs rely on Abel summation, product-to-sum identities, and bounding partial sums (2S_k = cos((m+1)/2 x) − cos((k+m+1)/2 x) so |S_k| ≤ 1). The lemmas give explicit uniform bounds used to conclude the desired inequality in Problem 51.
